key_insight: A differentiable overlapping Schwarz solver couples near-wall and bulk transport models, enabling inverse modeling of thin boundary layers with coarser meshes.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce computational costs when inferring spatially varying transport properties in high-Péclet-number engineering flows.
method: Discretize perturbation-based inner and outer transport equations with finite elements and couple them through overlapping Schwarz iterations.
Use adjoint sensitivities for inverse optimization, imposing governing equations and boundary conditions as hard constraints.
Integrate LLM-driven updates or a workflow-level AI agent that expands a functional basis under staged admission rules.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower computational cost than a single-domain formulation and greater agentic-AI benefit for functional-basis unknowns than nodal fields, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the unknown's representation and basis-admission policy; gains should not be assumed for high-dimensional nodal fields.
paper_title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
